A 24-year-old male with a history of chronic back pain, obesity, and hypertension seeks medical
attention for acute central back pain that began 3 days ago following an overnight work session. The
pain is position-dependent but non-radiating, with no additional symptoms. His vital signs are normal.
Physical examination reveals sharp tenderness and warmth around T5-T9, with the left transverse
process at T7 being notably softer and more yielding to anterior pressure compared to adjacent
vertebrae. The asymmetry of the transverse processes normalizes when the patient extends at this
segment. For treating this patient in a supine position using a single, rapid-force technique, which setup
and force direction would be most appropriate? Answer Choices: (A) Physician's thenar eminence on
left transverse process of T7 with directional force to the ground (B) Physician's thenar eminence on
right transverse process of T8 with directional force toward T9 (C) Physician's thenar eminence on right
transverse process of T7 with directional force toward T6 (D) Physician’s thenar eminence on right
transverse process of T7 with directional force toward T8 (E) Physician's thenar eminence on right
transverse process of T7 with directional force to the ground (F) Physician's thenar eminence on left
transverse process of T8 with directional force toward T7 (G) Physician's thenar eminence on left
transverse process of T6 with directional force to the ground (H) Physician's thenar eminence on right
transverse process of T6 with directional force toward T7 (I) Physician's thenar eminence on left
transverse process of T7 with directional force toward T6 (J) Physician's thenar eminence on left
transverse process of T8 with directional force to the ground
 A. Physician's thenar eminence on left transverse process of T7 with directional force to the ground
B. Physician’s thenar eminence on right transverse process of T7 with directional force toward T8
C. Physician's thenar eminence on right transverse process of T8 with directional force toward T9
D. Physician's thenar eminence on left transverse process of T8 with directional force to the ground
E. Physician's thenar eminence on left transverse process of T6 with directional force to the ground
F. Physician's thenar eminence on right transverse process of T6 with directional force toward T7
G. Physician's thenar eminence on left transverse process of T7 with directional force toward T6
H. Physician's thenar eminence on left transverse process of T8 with directional force toward T7
I. Physician's thenar eminence on right transverse process of T7 with directional force toward T6
J. Physician's thenar eminence on right transverse process of T7 with directional force to the ground
